Engineering Note: Waypoint Production Deployment Topology

The Waypoint dispatch backend runs on the Field Ops Compute Cluster, the compute node in our primary region that hosts everything below it. That cluster composes the DocumentDB Engine, the system software that runs our document storage, and the DocumentDB Engine realizes the Job Event Store Service, the technology service the rest of the platform calls to read and write job events.

The Field Ops Compute Cluster also composes the Waypoint Server Image, the deployed container artifact every node boots from; that image in turn realizes the Job Event Store Service, since the running service is only ever the image brought to life on the cluster.

Tying the region together is the Dispatch Backbone Network, the communication network our infrastructure runs over. It connects the Field Ops Compute Cluster to the rest of the region, serves the Technician Handset -- the field device each technician carries -- directly, and supports the Job Event Store Service so calls from the field reach the backend. The DocumentDB Engine uses the Dispatch Backbone Network for cross-node replication.

For resilience we model the two-region setup as the Regional Failover Collaboration, a technology collaboration that aggregates the Field Ops Compute Cluster, uses the Dispatch Backbone Network to stay in sync, and realizes the Job Event Store Service so the service survives a single region going dark. We assign the Dispatch Backbone Network to that collaboration, since the network is what the failover pair is built around.
